title: Canonical completed Jacobian presentation
statement: Let $k,F$ be fields and $A$ a commutative local $k$-algebra with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, completion $C=\widehat A$ as in [def-trf-formal-local-presentation], and $M=C\otimes_A\Omega_{A/k}$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Given integers $n,s\ge0$, a ring map $\Phi:F[[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and equations $f_1,\ldots,f_s$, say these give the canonical completed Jacobian presentation if there is a continuous $k$-derivation $D:C\to M$ extending $a\mapsto1\otimes da$, and a surjective $C$-linear map $\pi:C^n\to M$ with $\pi(e_i)=D(\Phi(t_i))$ and kernel the $C$-span of the columns $(\Phi(\partial f_j/\partial t_i))_{i=1}^n$ for $j=1,\ldots,s$. Continuity of $D$ means that for every $r\ge0$ some $N\ge0$ satisfies $D((\mathfrak mC)^N)\subseteq(\mathfrak mC)^rM$. Thus $M$ is the cokernel of the displayed Jacobian matrix with its specified differential map; tensor symmetry identifies $M$ with $\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A C$. This is a predicate, not an existence theorem.
